children.name: Derivatives Market Structures
Exchange-traded markets with standardized contracts
Over-the-counter private bilateral agreements
Central clearing counterparties to reduce systemic risk
Forward Contracts
Private OTC agreements for future delivery
Long position buyer pays delivery price
Short position seller delivers the asset
Payoffs realized only at contract maturity
Futures Contracts
Standardized agreements traded on organized exchanges
Daily settlement and margin account adjustments
Flexible range of specified delivery dates
Virtually no credit risk via clearinghouse
Options Contracts
Call options provide right to buy
Put options provide right to sell
American style allowing early exercise
European style exercisable only at maturity
Requires up-front premium payment
Hedgers
Objective to reduce existing risk exposure
Forwards neutralize risk by fixing prices
Options provide insurance with upside potential
Speculators
Betting on future price movements
Obtain high leverage through derivatives markets
Futures speculation carries unlimited loss potential
Options speculation limits loss to premium
Arbitrageurs
Locking in risk-free profit from mispricings
Simultaneous offsetting trades in multiple markets
Market forces rapidly eliminate arbitrage opportunities
